1. Purpose
This policy establishes the principles, criteria, and controls governing the recognition and measurement of Order
Intake across the Company.
2. Scope
This policy applies to all business units, regions, and legal entities that generate, process, or record customer orders
under the Order-to-Cash (O2C) cycle, including:
- Hardware and Software arrangements
- Standalone Services arrangements
- Bundled multi-element arrangements
3. Definitions
3.1 Order
A binding agreement between the Company and a customer under which the Company commits to deliver goods
and/or services in exchange for consideration.
3.2 Order Backlog
The cumulative value of Orders recognized as Order Intake but not yet delivered, fulfilled, or recognized as revenue.
4. Roles and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Sales Operations | Order capture and documentation collection
Finance Business Partners | Recognition criteria review
Finance Manager | Credit risk sign-off (see 5.3)
Group Finance (Revenue Assurance) | Policy ownership and testing
5. Order Intake Recognition and Measurement
5.1 Recognition Criteria for Order Intake
An order shall be recognized as Order Intake when:
- a) A legally binding contract or Purchase Order (PO) exists, AND
- b) The order value can be reliably measured.
Orders not meeting both (a) and (b) shall remain in the sales pipeline and shall not be recorded as Order Intake.
5.2 Customer Commitment
Customer commitment is evidenced by receipt of a signed Purchase Order alone. A countersigned contract is
preferred but not mandatory, provided the PO specifies:
- Price

5.3 Collectability Assessment
5.3.1 Assessment Basis
Collectability is assessed based solely on the customer's credit rating at time of order receipt, as classified below:
Credit Rating | Risk Classification | Action Required
A | Low Risk | None
B | Medium Risk | Standard booking
Below B | High Risk | Finance Manager review
5.3.2 Escalation Requirements
Orders from customers rated below "B" require Finance Manager sign-off prior to booking. No additional escalation is
required regardless of order value.
5.4 Timing for Booking of Order Intake
Order Intake shall be booked immediately upon receipt of a valid Purchase Order, regardless of contract signature
status. This approach prioritizes:
- Timeliness of reporting, over
- Administrative completeness of documentation
CONTROL PRINCIPLE
A valid Purchase Order is the primary trigger for Order Intake booking, subject to the recognition criteria and
collectability requirements defined above.
6. Order Intake Approvals
Refer to POL-ORD-003 (Order Intake Approval & Backlog Management Policy) for the applicable delegation of
authority matrix.
7. Exceptions and Escalation
Deviations from this policy require Finance Manager approval, with escalation to Group Finance for exceptions
exceeding $100,000 in order value.

- POL-ORD-002: Order Intake Value & SSP Allocation Policy
- POL-ORD-003: Order Intake Approval & Backlog Management Policy

1. Purpose
This policy establishes the principles, criteria, and controls governing the recognition and measurement of Order
Intake across the Company. This version supersedes v1.0 and introduces enhanced controls following the 2024
internal audit cycle.
2. Scope
This policy applies to all business units, regions, and legal entities that generate, process, or record customer orders
under the Order-to-Cash (O2C) cycle, including:
- Hardware and Software arrangements
- Standalone Services arrangements
- Bundled multi-element arrangements
3. Definitions
3.1 Order
A binding agreement between the Company and a customer, evidenced by BOTH a Purchase Order AND a
countersigned contract (see 5.2).
3.2 Order Backlog
The cumulative value of Orders recognized as Order Intake but not yet delivered, fulfilled, or recognized as revenue.
4. Roles and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Sales Operations | Order capture; ensures PO + contract obtained
Finance Business Partners | Recognition criteria review
Regional Finance Head | Risk sign-off (elevated from v1.0)
Group Treasury | Publishes month-end FX spot rates
Group Finance (Revenue Assurance) | Policy ownership and testing
5. Order Intake Recognition and Measurement
5.1 Recognition Criteria for Order Intake
An order shall be recognized as Order Intake when ALL of the following conditions are met:
- A legally binding contract or Purchase Order (PO) exists, AND
- The order value can be reliably measured, AND
- Collectability is reasonably assured (see 5.3).
KEY CHANGE FROM v1.0
Collectability is now a recognition precondition, not merely a downstream approval trigger.

5.2 Customer Commitment
Customer commitment must be evidenced by BOTH:
- A signed Purchase Order
- A countersigned contract
Orders supported by a PO alone do NOT qualify for recognition.
5.3 Collectability Assessment
5.3.1 Risk Scoring Model
Collectability is assessed using a combined weighted risk score:
Risk Score = (0.40 × Credit Rating Score) + (0.35 × Payment History Score) + (0.25 × Country Risk Score)
Each component is scored on a 0–100 scale. Credit Rating Score is derived from Group Credit Risk classification;
Payment History Score is based on trailing 12-month payment behavior; Country Risk Score is published quarterly by
Group Treasury.
Risk Score Range | Classification | Action Required
80–100 | Low Risk | None
50–79 | Medium Risk | Standard booking
Below 50 | High Risk | Regional Finance Head review
5.3.2 Escalation Requirements
Orders scoring below 50 require MANDATORY Regional Finance Head sign-off prior to booking.
5.4 Timing for Booking of Order Intake
Order Intake shall be booked ONLY once BOTH of the following are received and verified by Finance:
- Signed Purchase Order
- Countersigned contract
5.5 Orders in Non-Euro Currencies
5.5.1 Conversion Methodology
Converted Order Value (EUR) = Order Value (Local Currency) ÷ Month-End Spot Rate
The Month-End Spot Rate is published by Group Treasury as of the booking date.
5.5.2 FX Variance Control
-
FX Variance (%) = |Booking Rate Order Date Rate| ÷ Order Date Rate × 100
If FX Variance (%) > 5%, the order must be:
- Flagged in the system
- Routed to the Controller for review prior to final booking

1. Purpose
This policy defines the methodology used to measure the value of Order Intake for multi-element arrangements,
including allocation of contract value across deliverables using Standalone Selling Price (SSP).
2. Scope
Applies to all multi-element customer arrangements combining:
- Hardware/Software (HW/SW) deliverables, AND
- Services deliverables
3. Definitions
Standalone Selling Price (SSP): The price at which the Company would sell a deliverable separately under similar
circumstances.
4. Roles and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Deal Desk | Prepares SSP allocation calculations
Finance Manager | Reviews allocations exceeding variance threshold
Pricing Team | Maintains standard list price catalogue
5. SSP Allocation Methodology
5.1 Calculation Basis
Allocation is performed using the Standalone List Price method. Each deliverable is allocated a share of total contract
value based on its list price relative to total list price of all deliverables. No weighting adjustment is applied.
5.2 Allocation Formula
SSP Allocation (Deliverable) = (List Price of Deliverable ÷ Total List Price of All Deliverables) × Total Contract Value
6. Sample Allocation Illustration
Deliverable | Contract Value | SSP | SSP Allocation
HW/SW | 30 | 30 | 27.90
Services | 1 | 10 | 3.10
Total | 31 | 40 | 31.00
The allocation reflects a proportional split based on the list price ratio of 30:10, applied against total contract value of
31.

1. Purpose
This policy defines the methodology used to measure the value of Order Intake for multi-element arrangements. This
version supersedes v1.0 and introduces a weighted allocation methodology following Q1 2025 internal audit
recommendations.
2. Scope
Applies to all multi-element customer arrangements combining:
- Hardware/Software (HW/SW) deliverables, AND
- Services deliverables
3. Definitions
Standalone Selling Price (SSP): The price at which the Company would sell a deliverable separately under similar
circumstances.
Weighted Factor: An adjustment factor applied per deliverable category to reflect margin and risk differences,
determined annually by the Pricing Committee.
4. Roles and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Deal Desk | Prepares Relative SSP allocation calculations
Regional Finance Head | Reviews allocations exceeding threshold (elevated from Finance Manager)
Pricing Committee | Determines annual Weighted Factors
5. SSP Allocation Methodology
5.1 Calculation Basis
Allocation is performed using the Relative SSP method, under which a Weighted Factor is applied per deliverable
category. This replaces the unweighted Standalone List Price method used in v1.0.
5.2 Weighted Factor Determination
The Weighted Factor is determined annually by the Pricing Committee based on:
- Historical margin performance by deliverable category
- Delivery risk profile
- Market comparables
5.3 Allocation Formula
Step 1 — Relative SSP: Relative SSP = SSP × Weighted Factor
Step 2 — SSP Allocation: SSP Allocation = (Relative SSP ÷ Total Relative SSP) × Total Contract Value
Step 3 — Variance Check: SSP % from Contract Value = (SSP Allocation - Proportional Contract Value) ÷
Proportional Contract Value × 100

1. Purpose
This policy defines approval authority levels for booking Order Intake and establishes requirements for Order Backlog
monitoring.
2. Scope
Applies to all Orders booked as Order Intake and to periodic review of Order Backlog balances.
3. Approval Authority Matrix
Order Value | Approver
Up to $50,000 | Sales Manager
$50,001 – $250,000 | Regional Finance Head
Above $250,000 | CFO
Approval must be documented and retained in the order file.
4. Order Backlog Management
4.1 Review Frequency
Order Backlog is reviewed on a quarterly basis by the Finance team.
4.2 Aging Calculation
Aging (Days) = Current Date - Original Order Booking Date
4.3 Flagging Criteria
Backlog items shall be flagged for review when:
- Aging (Days) > 365 days (12 months), AND
- No delivery milestone has been recorded in the system
Flagged items require Finance Manager review to determine whether continued recognition remains appropriate.
5. Roles and Responsibilities
Role | Responsibility
Sales Manager | Approves orders up to $50,000
Regional Finance Head | Approves orders $50,001–$250,000
CFO | Approves orders above $250,000
Finance Team | Performs quarterly Backlog review
6. Related Policies
- POL-ORD-001: Order Intake Recognition & Measurement Policy

1. Audit Objective
To assess whether Order Intake was recognized and measured in accordance with POL-ORD-001 v1.0, and to
evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of related controls (CTRL-REV-014).
2. Background and Scope
This audit plan was developed for the FY2024 Q4 audit cycle, covering Order Intake transactions booked between
July 2024 and October 2024. Scope includes:
- Hardware/Software orders
- Standalone Services orders
- Bundled multi-element arrangements
3. Key Risk Indicators (KRIs)
KRI ID | KRI Description | Related Policy Clause | Risk Rating
KRI-001 | Orders recognized without valid PO or contract | Section 5.1 | High
KRI-002 | Orders booked based on PO only, without countersigned contra | ctSection 5.2 | Medium
KRI-003 | Orders from low credit-rated customers booked without required | sSigenc-toioffn 5.3.2 | High
KRI-004 | Order Intake booked prior to satisfying timing criteria | Section 5.4 | Medium
4. Audit Planning Steps
4.1 Step Mapping to Policy Clauses
Step # | Audit Step Description | Policy Clause Tested | Related KRI
1 | Verify existence of valid PO for sampled orders | 5.1 | KRI-001
2 | Confirm customer commitment evidenced by signed PO | 5.2 | KRI-002
3 | Review credit rating classification and Finance Manager sign-off for orde | rs5 .r3a.t1e,d 5 b.3e.l2ow B | KRI-003
4 | Confirm booking date aligns with PO receipt date | 5.4 | KRI-004
4.2 Sample Selection Approach
- Population: All orders booked Jul–Oct 2024 (n = 342)
- Sample size: 15 orders, judgmentally selected across 3 regions
- Stratification: Weighted toward orders >$50,000 and customers rated below B
5. Testing Procedures Performed
- Inspected PO documentation for existence and completeness
- Traced credit rating classification to Group Credit Risk system
- Recalculated booking date against PO receipt date per Section 5.4
- Verified Finance Manager sign-off where credit rating below B

Step 2: 2 orders were booked using PO only; no countersigned contract was on file at time of booking. This was
compliant under v1.0 but flagged as a forward-looking risk given dual-document practice trends.
Step 3: 1 order from a customer rated C was booked without documented Finance Manager sign-off. Root cause:
sign-off obtained verbally, not recorded in system.
7. Prior Period Recommendations
- Introduce a secondary commitment document requirement beyond PO alone
- Enhance credit risk assessment beyond single-factor credit rating to include payment history and country risk
- Formalize system-based sign-off workflow to eliminate verbal approval gaps
8. Forward-Looking Note for Next Cycle
Group Finance indicated a policy update to POL-ORD-001 was planned for Q1 2025, expected to address the
recommendations above. The next audit cycle should re-baseline testing against the updated policy and re-assess
KRI-002 and KRI-003 risk ratings.

1. Audit Objective
To assess whether SSP allocation for multi-element Order Intake arrangements was performed in accordance with
POL-ORD-002 v1.0 (Standalone List Price method), and to evaluate control CTRL-REV-015.
2. Background and Scope
This audit plan covers multi-element contracts (HW/SW + Services) booked as Order Intake between October 2024
and January 2025.
3. Key Risk Indicators (KRIs)
KRI ID | KRI Description | Related Policy Clause | Risk Rating
KRI-005 | SSP allocation not recalculated using approved list price method | Section 5.1, 5.2 | High
KRI-006 | Allocation variance >20% booked without Finance Manager sig | n-Soeffction 7 | High
KRI-007 | Incorrect deliverable categorization (HW/SW vs Services) | Section 2 | Medium
4. Audit Planning Steps
4.1 Step Mapping to Policy Clauses
Step # | Audit Step Description | Policy Clause Tested | Related KRI
1 | Recalculate SSP allocation using Standalone List Price formula | 5.2 | KRI-005
2 | Compare recalculated allocation to booked system values | 5.2, 6 | KRI-005
3 | Identify allocations with variance >20% and confirm sign-off | 7 | KRI-006
4 | Validate deliverable categorization against contract terms | 2 | KRI-007
4.2 Sample Selection Approach
- Population: Multi-element contracts booked Oct 2024–Jan 2025 (n = 58)
- Sample size: 10 contracts, judgmentally selected to include higher-value and higher-variance arrangements
5. Testing Procedures Performed
- Obtained standard list price catalogue from Pricing Team
- Recalculated SSP allocation using the approved formula
- Compared recalculated allocation to system-booked values
- For variances >20%, traced to Finance Manager sign-off evidence
6. Findings Summary

Contract ID | Deliverable | List Price | Recalculated Allocation | Booked Allocation | Variance
C-2041 | HW/SW | 30 | 27.90 | 27.90 | 0%
C-2041 | Services | 10 | 3.10 | 3.10 | 0%
C-2077 | HW/SW | 45 | 38.25 | 31.00 | -18.9%
C-2077 | Services | 15 | 12.75 | 20.00 | +56.9%
Overall: 8/10 contracts matched recalculation within tolerance; 2/10 exceeded the 20% threshold.
Exception: Contract C-2077 showed a 56.9% variance on Services with no documented Finance Manager sign-off,
representing a control breach under Section 7.
7. Prior Period Recommendations
- Transition from unweighted Standalone List Price to a weighted allocation approach
- Lower the sign-off variance threshold from 20% to a more conservative level
- Implement system-enforced sign-off workflow
8. Forward-Looking Note for Next Cycle
Group Finance was expected to publish an updated SSP allocation methodology introducing a Weighted Factor per
deliverable category later in 2025. The next cycle should re-baseline the recalculation approach using the new
Relative SSP formula and re-test the approval variance threshold.

1. Audit Objective
To assess compliance with the Order Intake Approval Authority Matrix and Order Backlog monitoring requirements
under POL-ORD-003 v1.0, and evaluate control CTRL-REV-016.
2. Background and Scope
This audit plan covers orders booked between January 2025 and May 2025 for approval matrix testing, and quarterly
Backlog review reports for Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 for aging testing.
3. Key Risk Indicators (KRIs)
KRI ID | KRI Description | Related Policy Clause | Risk Rating
KRI-008 | Orders approved by incorrect authority level relative to value | Section 3 | High
KRI-009 | Backlog items aging >12 months not flagged for review | Section 4.2, 4.3 | Medium
KRI-010 | Quarterly Backlog review not evidenced/performed on schedule | Section 4.1 | Medium
4. Audit Planning Steps
4.1 Step Mapping to Policy Clauses
Step # | Audit Step Description | Policy Clause Tested | Related KRI
1 | Verify order approver matches required authority level relative to value ti | e3r | KRI-008
2 | Recalculate Backlog aging and confirm items >365 days were flagged | 4.2, 4.3 | KRI-009
3 | Confirm quarterly Backlog review evidence exists for each quarter | 4.1 | KRI-010
4.2 Sample Selection Approach
- Approval testing population: Orders booked Jan–May 2025 (n = 210)
- Approval sample size: 20 orders, stratified across all 3 value tiers
- Backlog testing: All items in Backlog >300 days as of review date (n = 27), full population tested
5. Testing Procedures Performed
- Traced order value to approver identity and role in system
- Cross-referenced approver role against Table 1 (Delegation of Authority) in POL-ORD-003 v1.0
-
- Recalculated aging using Aging (Days) = Current Date Original Order Booking Date
- Confirmed items >365 days were flagged and reviewed by Finance Manager
- Obtained quarterly Backlog review sign-off evidence for Q4 2024 and Q1 2025
6. Findings Summary
6.1 Approval Matrix Testing
